title: Managed Host Connectivity - CRITICAL
observation: Managed Host Connectivity: Hosts in error/unreachable state: qr-ec01 (10.10.1.22) QRadar also raised 1 related notification(s), e.g. "Managed host qr-ec01 is not responding (hostcontext down)".
description: One or more managed hosts are unreachable from the Console or report an error/inactive state.
root_cause: Verify SSH/encryption tunnel (TCP 22/4333), hostcontext service and time sync on these hosts.
impact: Configuration cannot be deployed to the host; events/flows from that host may be missing; services may be down.
business_impact: Partial or complete loss of data from components on that host.
recommendation: Verify network connectivity and SSH from the Console to the managed host (TCP 22) and that the encryption tunnel (TCP 4333 / 7777) is established.
Check 'hostcontext' and 'tomcat' services on the managed host, system time (NTP) and disk space.
If the host was rebuilt, remove and re-add it, then deploy full configuration.
best_practice: Monitor managed host status and keep time synchronised across the deployment.

corroborating_notifications: Managed host qr-ec01 is not responding (hostcontext down)

title: EPS licence utilisation 144%
observation: EPS: licensed 25000, current 26886, peak 35987 (144% of licence). 12-month forecast 298%. QRadar also raised 1 related notification(s), e.g. "License EPS threshold exceeded: current 28,400 EPS exceeds licensed 25,000 EPS".
description: The events-per-second rate received by one or more event processors exceeded the licensed EPS pool or the per-host allocation.
impact: Events above the licensed rate are queued to the temporary 'burst' buffer and, when the buffer is exhausted, are dropped or routed to the 'Dropped Events' log source, causing detection and compliance gaps.
business_impact: Security telemetry is silently lost during peak periods; offenses may not fire and audit evidence can be incomplete.
risk: High - data loss and potential licence compliance breach.
recommendation: Review the License Pool Management page (Admin > System Configuration > System and License Management) and confirm EPS allocation per managed host.
Identify the top EPS log sources (Log Activity > Group by Log Source) and filter noisy or low-value events with routing rules, custom event properties or at-source tuning.
Rebalance EPS between event processors, or purchase additional EPS capacity / add an Event Processor.
Enable event coalescing for high-volume, repetitive sources and disable payload storage where not required.
best_practice: IBM recommends sizing EPS licence at 20-30% above sustained peak and reviewing consumption at least quarterly; avoid sustained operation above 90% of the licensed rate.

corroborating_notifications: License EPS threshold exceeded: current 28,400 EPS exceeds licensed 25,000 EPS

title: CPU utilisation on qr-console01
observation: [qr-console01] Average CPU 88.0% (p95 100.0%, peak 100.0%); saturated (>=90%) in 50.0% of samples.
description: CPU utilisation is sustained above healthy levels on one or more QRadar hosts.
root_cause: Event processing (ecs-ep / ecs-ec-ingress), Ariel searches, CRE rule evaluation or application containers are consuming available CPU capacity.
impact: Increased search latency, event processing delays and risk of event drops at the pipeline.
business_impact: Delayed detection and degraded analyst experience.
recommendation: Identify the processes with the highest CPU (ecs-ec-ingress, ecs-ep, ariel_proxy_server, postgres, java/tomcat, apps).
Review custom rules (CRE) and expensive custom properties; disable or optimise those that are CPU-heavy.
Redistribute event sources or add an Event/Flow Processor; consider upgrading appliance hardware.
best_practice: IBM sizing guidance targets sustained CPU below 70% with peaks below 90%.

title: Disk usage /var/log on qr-ep01
observation: [qr-ep01] /var/log is 96% full (48.0 GB of 50.0 GB). QRadar also raised 1 related notification(s), e.g. "Disk usage on /store has exceeded 93% on qr-ep01".
description: A monitored file system (/store, /storetmp, /var/log, /transient, /) has crossed the QRadar disk usage warning/critical threshold.
root_cause: Ariel data retention, backups, temporary files, core dumps or application volumes have filled the file system.
impact: At 95% QRadar stops accepting events and flows (ecs-ec-ingress / hostcontext halts services) and Ariel searches fail; /var/log or / full can crash PostgreSQL and tomcat.
business_impact: Event collection outage and loss of historical search; recovery requires emergency clean-up.
risk: Critical - service outage imminent or ongoing.
recommendation: Identify the largest consumers with 'du -shx /store/* | sort -h' and the /store/ariel retention settings.
Review Ariel retention buckets (Admin > Data Retention) and reduce retention for low-value event/flow categories.
Remove stale files in /store/tmp, /storetmp, old backups and large core/heap dumps; rotate /var/log.
Add storage (expand LVM volume, add a Data Node, or offload to a secondary store) and enable Data Node rebalancing.
Configure disk usage notification thresholds to alert at 80% / 90%.
best_practice: IBM recommends keeping /store below 80% with retention aligned to compliance; never run above 90% as the 95% hard stop halts processing.

corroborating_notifications: Disk usage on /store has exceeded 93% on qr-ep01

title: Application memory pressure: Pulse
observation: Pulse 2.2.1 on qr-apphost01: Memory at 96% of limit
description: One or more application containers are consuming memory close to their configured limit.
impact: Risk of OOM kills and restart loops, degraded application responsiveness.
recommendation: Raise the container memory limit if the host has capacity.
Redistribute applications across hosts or add an App Host.
best_practice: Keep application memory usage below 80% of the limit.

title: Application restart loop detected: ThreatIntel
observation: ThreatIntel 3.1.0 on qr-apphost01: Container restarted 14 times
description: An application container has restarted repeatedly, typically due to crashes, out-of-memory kills or failing health checks.
impact: Intermittent or failed application availability and consumption of host CPU/IO by crash loops.
business_impact: Unstable analyst tooling; potential impact on co-located workloads.
recommendation: Inspect container logs and 'docker inspect' for exit codes (137 = OOM kill).
Increase the application memory allocation (Admin > Apps > Manage > Resources) or move the app to a host with more RAM.
Update to the latest app release and raise a support case with logs if the loop continues.
best_practice: Review application resource consumption regularly and size the App Host according to the app sizing guide.

title: App Framework / container error: User Behavior Analytics
observation: User Behavior Analytics 4.1.2 on qr-apphost01: Application in error state: Container exited with code 137 (OOMKilled) QRadar also raised 1 related notification(s), e.g. "Application ThreatIntel container restarted unexpectedly".
description: The QRadar Apps Framework (Docker) reports failures starting, installing or running an application container.
impact: Installed applications (e.g. Log Source Management, Pulse, UBA, Use Case Manager) are unavailable.
business_impact: Features relying on the application are unavailable to analysts.
recommendation: Check container state with 'docker ps -a' and logs with 'docker logs <id>' on the App Host/Console.
Validate free space on /store/docker and on the application volume; verify the Docker service and 'qrd' services.
Re-deploy the application or restart via Admin > Apps; verify the minimum QRadar version for the application.
best_practice: Dedicate an App Host for production workloads (>3 applications) and keep apps on supported versions.

title: DSM / protocol error on log sources
observation: 15 of 140 log sources (10.7%) are in ERROR state.
description: A device support module or protocol integration reports errors (connection, credential, format or version mismatch).
impact: Events from the affected log source are missing, delayed or incorrectly normalised.
business_impact: Monitoring gap for the affected technology.
recommendation: Open the log source in Log Source Management and review the status message and the protocol-specific diagnostics (Test Connection).
Verify credentials, firewall rules and certificate validity for the integration; update the DSM and protocol RPMs through Auto Update.
Resolve duplicate / misconfigured log source identifiers if the same device is mapped twice.
best_practice: Monitor log source status centrally and remediate ERROR sources within 5 business days; use the Log Source Management app's bulk tools.

title: Event parsing errors / unparsed events
observation: 12 log source(s) are typed as Unknown/Generic, indicating missing or incorrect DSM mapping. QRadar also raised 1 related notification(s), e.g. "Events were not parsed: Unknown log source type for 14 sources".
description: A significant share of events are unrecognised (Unknown/Stored events) or raise parsing exceptions in the event pipeline.
impact: Events are stored with generic categories, cannot be used in CRE rules and searches, and consume licence and storage without security value.
business_impact: Detections and compliance reports miss data from the affected sources.
recommendation: Use Log Activity > filter 'Log Source Type = Unknown' / 'Event Name = Unknown' to identify the sources.
Install the correct DSM and latest DSM/protocol Auto Update; confirm the log source type and protocol settings.
Where no DSM exists, use the DSM Editor / Universal DSM with LEEF/CEF formatting.
Review 'Parsing Issues' notifications and /var/log/qradar.error for exceptions.
best_practice: Keep Unknown/Stored events below 1% of total; review parsing health monthly using the Log Source Management app.

corroborating_notifications: Events were not parsed: Unknown log source type for 14 sources

title: CPU I/O wait on qr-console01
description: The CPU spends significant time waiting for disk I/O.
root_cause: CPU threads are blocked waiting for storage; usually slow disks, heavy Ariel searches or retention/cleanup jobs.
impact: Indicates storage latency or contention; delays event commit and search execution.
recommendation: Review storage subsystem health and latency.
Reduce concurrent heavy Ariel searches/reports; review retention.
best_practice: Sustained iowait above 10% is a sign of storage contention.

title: Disk await dev8-0 on qr-console01
observation: [qr-console01] Storage latency on dev8-0: await avg 47.6 ms (peak 70 ms); r_await 0.0 ms, w_await 0.0 ms; avgqu-sz 5.95.
description: Average disk request latency (await / r_await / w_await) is above the healthy range for the QRadar workload.
root_cause: Storage subsystem cannot service request queue fast enough (shared SAN latency, RAID rebuild, saturated spindles, noisy neighbours or heavy Ariel searches).
impact: Slow Ariel writes and searches, ingestion queue growth, delayed offenses and high I/O wait on CPU.
business_impact: Analysts experience slow searches and late detections; risk of event backlog and drops.
risk: High - storage subsystem is a throughput bottleneck.
recommendation: Review the storage subsystem (SAN/NAS latency, RAID health, cache battery, queue depth, multipath).
Review data retention settings and large scheduled Ariel searches / reports running during ingestion peaks.
Review application storage use (App Framework volumes on /store) and move heavy apps to a dedicated App Host.
For virtual appliances ensure thick-provisioned, SSD-backed datastores and dedicated I/O paths.
best_practice: IBM storage guidance targets average await < 10 ms for /store (SSD < 2 ms); sustained values above 20 ms indicate a storage bottleneck.

evidence.threshold: warn >=10 ms, high >=20 ms, critical >=50 ms
